Use screenshots for visual facts the semantic tree cannot express;\\nuse coordinate input only as a fallback. Report automated and manual evidence\\nseparately.\\n\\n## Performance rules\\n\\n- Do not mutate state or notify unconditionally in `render`.\\n- Avoid rebuilding entities, subscriptions, focus handles, and expensive data\\n  structures per frame.\\n- Notify the narrowest owning entity after a coherent state change.\\n- Virtualize long collections and render only the visible range.\\n- Avoid cloning large strings or collections solely to satisfy a closure;\\n  capture stable handles or shared data.\\n- Measure before adding caches. A cache must have a clear invalidation owner.\\n- Keep animation work bounded and honor reduced motion.\\n\\n## Common failure modes\\n\\nAvoid these patterns:\\n\\n- one entity containing the entire application's unrelated state;\\n- business logic and network requests embedded in a long `render` method;\\n- random or index-based `ElementId` values for reorderable content;\\n- literal colors and radii that break custom themes;\\n- custom clickable `div`s where a semantic component already supplies focus,\\n  keyboard, disabled, and accessibility behavior;\\n- duplicated local state that drifts from a controlled model value;\\n- `cx.notify()` loops caused by mutation during every render;\\n- nested scroll containers without explicit ownership;\\n- a new component variant for a one-off screen;\\n- confirmation dialogs for reversible, low-risk actions;\\n- tests that call internal methods but never exercise keyboard or pointer\\n  behavior.\\n\\n## Rules for coding agents\\n\\nBefore editing, an agent must read the nearest implementation, its tests, the\\nre-export seam, and the relevant component documentation. fix all warnings before finalising\\n\\n## Reference Guide\\n\\nLoad detailed guidance based on context:\\n\\n| Topic | Reference | Load When |\\n|-------|-----------|-----------|\\n| Ownership | `references/ownership.md` | Lifetimes, borrowing, smart pointers, Pin |\\n| Traits | `references/traits.md` | Trait design, generics, associated types, derive |\\n| Error Handling | `references/error-handling.md` | Result, Option, ?, custom errors, thiserror |\\n| Async | `references/async.md` | async/await, tokio, futures, streams, concurrency |\\n| Testing | `references/testing.md` | Unit/integration tests, proptest, benchmarks |\\n\\n## Key Patterns with Examples\\n\\n### Ownership & Lifetimes\\n\\n```rust\\n// Explicit lifetime annotation — borrow lives as long as the input slice\\nfn longest<'a>(x: &'a str, y: &'a str) -> &'a str {\\n    if x.len() > y.len() { x } else { y }\\n}\\n\\n// Prefer borrowing over cloning\\nfn process(data: &[u8]) -> usize {   // &[u8] not Vec<u8>\\n    data.iter().filter(|&&b| b != 0).count()\\n}\\n```\\n\\n### Trait-Based Design\\n\\n```rust\\nuse std::fmt;\\n\\ntrait Summary {\\n    fn summarise(&self) -> String;\\n    fn preview(&self) -> String {          // default implementation\\n        format!(\\\"{}...\\\", &self.summarise()[..50])\\n    }\\n}\\n\\n#[derive(Debug)]\\nstruct Article { title: String, body: String }\\n\\nimpl Summary for Article {\\n    fn summarise(&self) -> String {\\n        format!(\\\"{}: {}\\\", self.title, self.body)\\n    }\\n}\\n```\\n\\n### Error Handling with `thiserror`\\n\\n```rust\\nuse thiserror::Error;\\n\\n#[derive(Debug, Error)]\\npub enum AppError {\\n    #[error(\\\"I/O error: {0}\\\")]\\n    Io(#[from] std::io::Error),\\n    #[error(\\\"parse error for value `{value}`: {reason}\\\")]\\n    Parse { value: String, reason: String },\\n}\\n\\n// ? propagates errors ergonomically\\nfn read_config(path: &str) -> Result<String, AppError> {\\n    let content = std::fs::read_to_string(path)?;  // Io variant via #[from]\\n    Ok(content)\\n}\\n```\\n\\n### Async / Await with Tokio\\n\\n```rust\\nuse tokio::time::{sleep, Duration};\\n\\n#[tokio::main]\\nasync fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {\\n    let result = fetch_data(\\\"https://example.com\\\").await?;\\n    println!(\\\"{result}\\\");\\n    Ok(())\\n}\\n\\nasync fn fetch_data(url: &str) -> Result<String, reqwest::Error> {\\n    let body = reqwest::get(url).await?.text().await?;\\n    Ok(body)\\n}\\n\\n// Spawn concurrent tasks — never mix blocking calls into async context\\nasync fn parallel_work() {\\n    let (a, b) = tokio::join!(\\n        sleep(Duration::from_millis(100)),\\n        sleep(Duration::from_millis(100)),\\n    );\\n}\\n```\\n\\n### Validation Commands\\n\\n```bash\\ncargo fmt --check                          # style check\\ncargo clippy --all-targets --all-features  # lints\\ncargo test                                 # unit + integration tests\\ncargo test --doc                           # doctests\\ncargo bench                                # criterion benchmarks (if present)\\n```\\n\\n## Constraints\\n\\n### MUST DO\\n- Use ownership and borrowing for memory safety\\n- Minimize unsafe code (document all unsafe blocks with safety invariants)\\n- Use type system for compile-time guarantees\\n- Handle all errors explicitly (`Result`/`Option`)\\n- Add comprehensive documentation with examples\\n- Run `cargo clippy` and fix all warnings\\n- Use `cargo fmt` for consistent formatting\\n- Write tests including doctests\\n\\n### MUST NOT DO\\n- Use `unwrap()` in production code (prefer `expect()` with messages)\\n- Create memory leaks or dangling pointers\\n- Use `unsafe` without documenting safety invariants\\n- Ignore clippy warnings\\n- Mix blocking and async code incorrectly\\n- Skip error handling\\n- Use `String` when `&str` suffices\\n- Clone unnecessarily (use borrowing)\\n\\n## Output Templates\\n\\nWhen implementing Rust features, provide:\\n1. One current code path stands out: the UI can retain “Setup complete” after a later setup check reports false, provided the selected installation hasn’t changed. That deserves a targeted reproduction because it fits the stale reassurance you reported.

The app already has shared summaries for folder and artwork state. I’d build on those, make failed checks invalidate stale success, and keep the next useful action beside the affected status.

truncated output (original token count: 2542)\\nTotal output lines: 169\\n\\n# RomMFS\\n\\nRomMFS connects your RomM library to a folder on your Windows PC. RetroBat or\\nanother emulator reads games from that folder. The first read downloads the\\nfile; subsequent reads use cached data. Your library stays on your RomM server.\\n\\n## Everyday use\\n\\nOpen **Overview** to see whether your games are available and what needs your\\nattention. Choose **Make games available**, then open RetroBat or your emulator\\nto play. Keep RomMFS running for the games folder to remain available.\\n\\n| Screen | Use it to |\\n|---|---|\\n| **Overview** | Start or stop the games folder, open it, and check library, RetroBat, save, and artwork status. |\\n| **Saves** | Turn on automatic save sync, see your saves, and review changes that need a decision. |\\n| **Activity** | See current work and recent results. Expand **Technical log** when troubleshooting. |\\n| **Settings** | Change your connection, folder, RetroBat installation, and application preferences. |\\n\\n- **Available** means the games folder is ready to use. It does not mean every\\n  game has been downloaded or is ready for offline play.\\n- **Library changes are ready** means RomMFS found a library update. Finish\\n  playing before choosing **Apply library changes**, which restarts the folder.\\n- **Artwork: Updating…** includes checking images and writing game information\\n  into RetroBat. Finished image checks do not mean the whole update is finished.\\n- **Artwork: Waiting for access** means RetroBat files are unavailable for the\\n  update. Close RetroBat or its emulators if they are open. RomMFS retries\\n  automatically; the games folder can remain available while it waits.\\n- **Saves: Off** means automatic save sync is disabled. Enable it in **Saves**\\n  after selecting the save folder or RetroBat installation you want to use.\\n\\n**Folder settings** on Overview opens the place to change your games folder.\\nSome settings require stopping the folder first; the page explains this and\\nprovides **Stop games folder**. Finish playing before stopping it.\\n\\nIf an action fails, read its explanation and use the nearby action to recover.\\n**Technical details** keeps the full diagnostic message available to copy.\\n\\n## Build and compatibility\\n\\nBuilt as a Rust workspace; uses Windows' built-in **Cloud Files API (CFAPI)**\\nthrough a custom `windows-sys` adapter and shows one small **GPUI** window.\\n## Set up RetroBat\\n\\n> RomM games appear alongside your own ROMs. RomMFS never moves, replaces or\\n> deletes anything already in RetroBat's `roms` folder, including the games\\n> and gamelists a fresh RetroBat install ships.\\n\\nIn the **Settings → RetroBat** tab, use **Download official installer** and then\\n**Launch installer…**, or select an installation you installed separately. Start RetroBat once and\\nclose it before setup so it creates its system configuration.\\nRomMFS discovers the latest stable official Windows package, streams its bytes,\\nchecks the release size and SHA-256 digest, and rechecks integrity before launch.\\nCancel a download in RomMFS; cancel installation inside the official wizard.\\nRomMFS does not guess unattended switches, terminate a writing installer, or\\nremove partial installation files. Stop RetroBat and its emulators before setup.\\nCompatible versions are accepted by required layout,\\nnot version equality; 8.2.1 is the source/package research reference.\\n\\nIn **Settings → Games folder**, select RetroBat, choose its installation and a\\nseparate managed ROM folder, then choose **Set up RetroBat** in the **RetroBat**\\ntab. For each system RetroBat defines,\\nsetup adds one folder link, `roms/<system>/RomM` → `<managed folder>/<system>`.\\n`roms/<system>` stays a real folder holding your own files; setup creates it\\nonly when RetroBat has none. A system that can't be linked (its folder is a link\\nor file of your own, or it already has something named `RomM`) is skipped with\\nthe reason, and the other systems are still linked. Switch save settings are\\nconfigured where possible; a problem there is reported and never blocks linking.\\n\\nWindows needs permission to create folder links. Setup checks this before\\nchanging anything and asks through UAC when needed; declining the prompt\\nleaves RetroBat exactly as it was.\\n\\nSetup records what it did in `<RetroBat>/.rommfs-setup.json`. Rerunning adds\\nlinks for newly available systems and restores removed ones. Changing the games\\nfolder or server and rerunning moves RomMFS's own links to the new target.\\nInstalls from earlier versions are converted: a `roms` or `roms/<system>` link\\nRomMFS created becomes a real folder again, and any folder an earlier version\\nmoved to `.rommfs-original-roms` is moved back. Targeted frontend settings edits\\nget an `es_settings.cfg.rommfs-<id>.bak` backup. The system-level Switch save\\noption is enabled; RetroBat's Eden/Citron launchers then generate their distinct\\nsave-location keys.\\n\\nMounting merges RomM games into each linked system's own\\n`roms/<system>/gamelist.xml`, under `./RomM/…` paths. Entries and folders RomMFS\\ndoesn't own are k…42 tokens truncated…on\\n\\n## Product polish — 26 October 2026\\n\\nThis pass improves the existing working application without requiring another\\nhuman test round before making UX changes.\\n\\n- Overview now uses readable, full-width sections for games, RetroBat, saves,\\n  and artwork. Primary actions wrap at smaller window sizes; library counts\\n  and optional details no longer compete with the main task.\\n- Artwork checking, publication, waiting for file access, failure, and success\\n  share one event-derived summary across Overview and Activity. Completing\\n  image checks no longer looks like completing the whole update. Waiting has\\n  an explanation and no animated progress bar.\\n- Errors use the shared plain-language explanations with full diagnostics\\n  behind Technical details. Folder settings opens the actual settings page;\\n  setup and locked settings explain the next available action.\\n- The window restores focus to the visible tab order when a page change\\n  removes the focused control. Native Tab and Enter navigation now survives\\n  transitions from setup to Overview and Settings.\\n- The README explains the roles of RomM, RomMFS, and RetroBat. The user guide\\n  starts with everyday tasks; the architecture guide explains how to follow a\\n  user action through the code.\\n\\nVerification: **385 portable tests passed**, including new coverage for\\nartwork publication/waiting/failure transitions and the unverified-save\\nexplanation. Formatting, host UI compilation, portable Clippy, and UI-enabled\\nClippy passed. Rendered the native GPUI screens in an isolated Linux/Xvfb\\nsource copy with seeded state at 1160×920 and 720×480. Checked disclosures,\\nfolder-settings navigation, and keyboard activation with assertions, and\\ninspected setup, Overview, Saves, Activity, Settings, and artwork progress,\\nwaiting, and failure states.\\n\\nThe preview used isolated settings and an inert event drain. These checks\\ncover presentation and navigation; they are not a new Windows runtime run.\\nThey do not establish the cause of file locks, deleted RetroBat links, or the\\nreported Windows latency. Mount ownership, lazy ROM reads, save consent, and\\nworker behavior retain their existing contracts.\\n\\n## Implementation progress — 17 October 2026\\n\\nCurrent step: implementation complete; native Windows acceptance remains outstanding. This record describes the working tree\\nbased on `55b5c104953a16dd9e3234bdd8588a8ff450eb9e`; it is not native Windows\\nacceptance. All save scenarios use temporary copies and the in-process fixture.\\nLive consent and live server data have not been changed.\\n\\n### Implementation and ownership\\n\\n- `crates/rommfs-app/src/controller/state.rs` owns event-derived folder,\\n  consent, scan and save summaries. `window.rs` drains events on the existing\\n  UI timer and notifies the visible page; `session.rs` retains application\\n  ownership independently of the window.\\n- `window/actions.rs` and `window/folder_controls.rs` dispatch Start, Stop,\\n  library checking and applying library changes. Start prepares placeholders;\\n  Stop disconnects the provider and cleans verified owned entries while\\n  retaining private cache and ordinary frontend metadata. Applying library\\n  changes runs that existing stop/start sequence. Catalogue checks stage a\\n  new snapshot separately from the active mount.\\n- `save_sync_agent/actor.rs` emits authoritative queue snapshots. A local\\n  watcher hint can finish without a new snapshot; that drain now emits its\\n  own queue update. Current per-save work comes from scheduler, dispatched\\n  revisions, reconciliation and journal baselines. Retained review versions\\n  are not queued downloads. Completed stages share revision identity in UI\\n  history and do not create work on restart.\\n- `controller/save_sync_setup.rs` owns persisted consent and save checks.\\n  Check for changes rediscovers/reconciles using the existing consent; it can\\n  transfer saves when consent is On and cannot enable consent when Off.\\n  Session IDs reject old worker results. An explicit pending consent change\\n  cannot be undone by the previous session's discovery response.\\n- `window/pages/overview.rs`, `save_review.rs`, `activity.rs` and `settings.rs`\\n  compose the four destinations. Supported save identities stay separate;\\n  remote review records nest beneath their owning identity. Skipped files\\n  have a separate disclosure; recorded replacement backups use journal\\n  evidence for their label, rather than filename-based ownership claims.\\n- `desktop.rs` opens the configured absolute folder through the native shell\\n  with a separate path argument and reports failure inline. It never falls\\n  back to the home or working directory.\\n- `Controller::begin_shutdown` requests cleanup once and transfers its join\\n  handle. Explicit tray Quit shows the closing state and joins off the UI\\n  thread before exiting. Window close still hides to the tray when a tray\\n  exists. The app-quit fallback also waits for cleanup off-thread.\\n- `controller/retrobat_setup.rs` runs metadata publication. Core setup-record\\n\"}}"}]

truncated output (original token count: 2542)\\nTotal output lines: 169\\n\\n# RomMFS\\n\\nRomMFS connects your RomM library to a folder on your Windows PC. RetroBat or\\nanother emulator reads games from that folder. The first read downloads the\\nfile; subsequent reads use cached data. Your library stays on your RomM server.\\n\\n## Everyday use\\n\\nOpen **Overview** to see whether your games are available and what needs your\\nattention. Choose **Make games available**, then open RetroBat or your emulator\\nto play. Keep RomMFS running for the games folder to remain available.\\n\\n| Screen | Use it to |\\n|---|---|\\n| **Overview** | Start or stop the games folder, open it, and check library, RetroBat, save, and artwork status. |\\n| **Saves** | Turn on automatic save sync, see your saves, and review changes that need a decision. |\\n| **Activity** | See current work and recent results. Expand **Technical log** when troubleshooting. |\\n| **Settings** | Change your connection, folder, RetroBat installation, and application preferences. |\\n\\n- **Available** means the games folder is ready to use. It does not mean every\\n  game has been downloaded or is ready for offline play.\\n- **Library changes are ready** means RomMFS found a library update. Finish\\n  playing before choosing **Apply library changes**, which restarts the folder.\\n- **Artwork: Updating…** includes checking images and writing game information\\n  into RetroBat. Finished image checks do not mean the whole update is finished.\\n- **Artwork: Waiting for access** means RetroBat files are unavailable for the\\n  update. Close RetroBat or its emulators if they are open. RomMFS retries\\n  automatically; the games folder can remain available while it waits.\\n- **Saves: Off** means automatic save sync is disabled. Enable it in **Saves**\\n  after selecting the save folder or RetroBat installation you want to use.\\n\\n**Folder settings** on Overview opens the place to change your games folder.\\nSome settings require stopping the folder first; the page explains this and\\nprovides **Stop games folder**. Finish playing before stopping it.\\n\\nIf an action fails, read its explanation and use the nearby action to recover.\\n**Technical details** keeps the full diagnostic message available to copy.\\n\\n## Build and compatibility\\n\\nBuilt as a Rust workspace; uses Windows' built-in **Cloud Files API (CFAPI)**\\nthrough a custom `windows-sys` adapter and shows one small **GPUI** window.\\n## Set up RetroBat\\n\\n> RomM games appear alongside your own ROMs. RomMFS never moves, replaces or\\n> deletes anything already in RetroBat's `roms` folder, including the games\\n> and gamelists a fresh RetroBat install ships.\\n\\nIn the **Settings → RetroBat** tab, use **Download official installer** and then\\n**Launch installer…**, or select an installation you installed separately. Start RetroBat once and\\nclose it before setup so it creates its system configuration.\\nRomMFS discovers the latest stable official Windows package, streams its bytes,\\nchecks the release size and SHA-256 digest, and rechecks integrity before launch.\\nCancel a download in RomMFS; cancel installation inside the official wizard.\\nRomMFS does not guess unattended switches, terminate a writing installer, or\\nremove partial installation files. Stop RetroBat and its emulators before setup.\\nCompatible versions are accepted by required layout,\\nnot version equality; 8.2.1 is the source/package research reference.\\n\\nIn **Settings → Games folder**, select RetroBat, choose its installation and a\\nseparate managed ROM folder, then choose **Set up RetroBat** in the **RetroBat**\\ntab. For each system RetroBat defines,\\nsetup adds one folder link, `roms/<system>/RomM` → `<managed folder>/<system>`.\\n`roms/<system>` stays a real folder holding your own files; setup creates it\\nonly when RetroBat has none. A system that can't be linked (its folder is a link\\nor file of your own, or it already has something named `RomM`) is skipped with\\nthe reason, and the other systems are still linked. Switch save settings are\\nconfigured where possible; a problem there is reported and never blocks linking.\\n\\nWindows needs permission to create folder links. Setup checks this before\\nchanging anything and asks through UAC when needed; declining the prompt\\nleaves RetroBat exactly as it was.\\n\\nSetup records what it did in `<RetroBat>/.rommfs-setup.json`. Rerunning adds\\nlinks for newly available systems and restores removed ones. Changing the games\\nfolder or server and rerunning moves RomMFS's own links to the new target.\\nInstalls from earlier versions are converted: a `roms` or `roms/<system>` link\\nRomMFS created becomes a real folder again, and any folder an earlier version\\nmoved to `.rommfs-original-roms` is moved back. Targeted frontend settings edits\\nget an `es_settings.cfg.rommfs-<id>.bak` backup. The system-level Switch save\\noption is enabled; RetroBat's Eden/Citron launchers then generate their distinct\\nsave-location keys.\\n\\nMounting merges RomM games into each linked system's own\\n`roms/<system>/gamelist.xml`, under `./RomM/…` paths. Entries and folders RomMFS\\ndoesn't own are k…42 tokens truncated…on\\n\\n## Product polish — 26 October 2026\\n\\nThis pass improves the existing working application without requiring another\\nhuman test round before making UX changes.\\n\\n- Overview now uses readable, full-width sections for games, RetroBat, saves,\\n  and artwork. Primary actions wrap at smaller window sizes; library counts\\n  and optional details no longer compete with the main task.\\n- Artwork checking, publication, waiting for file access, failure, and success\\n  share one event-derived summary across Overview and Activity. Completing\\n  image checks no longer looks like completing the whole update. Waiting has\\n  an explanation and no animated progress bar.\\n- Errors use the shared plain-language explanations with full diagnostics\\n  behind Technical details. Folder settings opens the actual settings page;\\n  setup and locked settings explain the next available action.\\n- The window restores focus to the visible tab order when a page change\\n  removes the focused control. Native Tab and Enter navigation now survives\\n  transitions from setup to Overview and Settings.\\n- The README explains the roles of RomM, RomMFS, and RetroBat. Checked disclosures,\\nfolder-settings navigation, and keyboard activation with assertions, and\\ninspected setup, Overview, Saves, Activity, Settings, and artwork progress,\\nwaiting, and failure states.\\n\\nThe preview used isolated settings and an inert event drain. These checks\\ncover presentation and navigation; they are not a new Windows runtime run.\\nThey do not establish the cause of file locks, deleted RetroBat links, or the\\nreported Windows latency. Mount ownership, lazy ROM reads, save consent, and\\nworker behavior retain their existing contracts.\\n\\n## Implementation progress — 17 October 2026\\n\\nCurrent step: implementation complete; native Windows acceptance remains outstanding. This record describes the working tree\\nbased on `55b5c104953a16dd9e3234bdd8588a8ff450eb9e`; it is not native Windows\\nacceptance. All save scenarios use temporary copies and the in-process fixture.\\nLive consent and live server data have not been changed.\\n\\n### Implementation and ownership\\n\\n- `crates/rommfs-app/src/controller/state.rs` owns event-derived folder,\\n  consent, scan and save summaries. `window.rs` drains events on the existing\\n  UI timer and notifies the visible page; `session.rs` retains application\\n  ownership independently of the window.\\n- `window/actions.rs` and `window/folder_controls.rs` dispatch Start, Stop,\\n  library checking and applying library changes. Start prepares placeholders;\\n  Stop disconnects the provider and cleans verified owned entries while\\n  retaining private cache and ordinary frontend metadata. Applying library\\n  changes runs that existing stop/start sequence. Catalogue checks stage a\\n  new snapshot separately from the active mount.\\n- `save_sync_agent/actor.rs` emits authoritative queue snapshots. A local\\n  watcher hint can finish without a new snapshot; that drain now emits its\\n  own queue update. Current per-save work comes from scheduler, dispatched\\n  revisions, reconciliation and journal baselines. Retained review versions\\n  are not queued downloads. Completed stages share revision identity in UI\\n  history and do not create work on restart.\\n- `controller/save_sync_setup.rs` owns persisted consent and save checks.\\n  Check for changes rediscovers/reconciles using the existing consent; it can\\n  transfer saves when consent is On and cannot enable consent when Off.\\n  Session IDs reject old worker results. An explicit pending consent change\\n  cannot be undone by the previous session's discovery response.\\n- `window/pages/overview.rs`, `save_review.rs`, `activity.rs` and `settings.rs`\\n  compose the four destinations. Supported save identities stay separate;\\n  remote review records nest beneath their owning identity. Skipped files\\n  have a separate disclosure; recorded replacement backups use journal\\n  evidence for their label, rather than filename-based ownership claims.\\n- `desktop.rs` opens the configured absolute folder through the native shell\\n  with a separate path argument and reports failure inline. It never falls\\n  back to the home or working directory.\\n- `Controller::begin_shutdown` requests cleanup once and transfers its join\\n  handle. Explicit tray Quit shows the closing state and joins off the UI\\n  thread before exiting. Window close still hides to the tray when a tray\\n  exists. **We get there by defining one dependable daily journey, freezing feature work, and spending the two days making that journey trustworthy on Windows.** A usable release candidate is a reasonable target. Calling every integration finished needs evidence we don’t yet have.

My read is that you dislike using it because **you have to interpret the application’s internal state before you can trust it.** You want to play games; the app asks you to reconcile connection, folder availability, RetroBat configuration, artwork publication, library changes, and save review. It leaves you asking: “Can I play? Is something broken? Am I supposed to wait or do something?”

I reviewed the current code, recent test notes, and captured screens. There are concrete reasons for that feeling:

- **“Setup complete” describes past configuration more reliably than present health.** The setup verifier explicitly doesn’t check individual RetroBat links. The UI also preserves earlier setup success when the same installation remains selected. That helps explain the report that removing a `RomM` link leaves everything looking fine. The project already has deeper link inspection we can reuse. See [setup verification](/home/aaron/Code/romm-fs/crates/rommfs-core/src/retrobat/setup.rs:226) and [retained setup state](/home/aaron/Code/romm-fs/crates/rommfs-app/src/controller/state.rs:602).
- **A blocked operation can leave you without a useful next step.** The file-access guard opens RetroBat executables exclusively. Failure establishes that access is unavailable; it doesn’t establish that you launched RetroBat. The recovery needs to reflect that uncertainty and handle the actual cause. See [the access guard](/home/aaron/Code/romm-fs/crates/rommfs-app/src/controller.rs:1070).
- **Recent polish has stronger presentation evidence than runtime evidence.** The latest remediation record reports portable tests and rendered screens, but explicitly leaves Windows latency, file locks, and deleted links unresolved. Another visual pass alone won’t close those gaps. See [verification limits](/home/aaron/Code/romm-fs/docs/ux-remediation.md:25).

The artwork contradiction has already received a shared state summary and transition tests. We should test that change on Windows before replacing it again.

**The release boundary**

I’m assuming the deadline means reliable everyday Windows + RetroBat use:

&gt; Connect once → connect RetroBat → make games available → find and play a supported game → close and reopen everything without repeating setup.

Artwork should update without making the application unpleasant to use. Optional sync should remain opt-in, with failures contained and understandable. Existing saves, local games, consent, and ownership protections remain mandatory.

Keep the current toolkit, backend, and navigation. Freeze new capabilities, broad refactors, and cosmetic redesigns.

**The two-day plan**

| Time | Work | Required result |
|---|---|---|
| **Day 1, first 2 hours** | Run the current build on the Windows machine where it feels bad. Walk through setup, normal startup, artwork updating, and playing. Capture timings and CPU/I/O activity. | A short ranked defect list with repeatable steps. Separate UI lag, slow operations, and confusing feedback. |
| **Day 1, next 4 hours** | Fix state truth and recovery at their existing owners: current RetroBat link health, artwork waiting/completion, and the next action after failure. | Overview answers whether games are available, what is blocked, and what action is useful. The same facts agree across pages. |
| **Day 1, final 2 hours** | Fix the largest measured responsiveness problem. Inspect UI event/render work, controller stalls, or filesystem activity according to the capture. | The reproduced interaction improves under the same conditions. Record anything still unresolved. |
| **Day 2, first 4 hours** | Exercise the complete journey on Windows, including representative failures. Fix release blockers and add focused behavior tests. | Fresh setup and returning use both work; failures recover without resetting configuration or risking files. |
| **Day 2, final 4 hours** | Stop expanding scope. Run the required checks, retest the candidate, package it, and reconcile the user guide with actual behavior. | One identifiable build, an acceptance record, and a short list of known limitations. |

Windows access belongs at the beginning. Leaving it until the end would repeat the largest gap in the existing evidence.

**What the interface needs to achieve**

Each screen should make three things obvious: **what works now, what needs attention, and what happens next.**

“Games available; artwork waiting for file access; save sync off” can be a perfectly valid situation. Those facts need clear scope and priority. A spinner should mean work is advancing or awaiting a response; a blocked operation needs an explanation. A previous successful setup should remain distinguishable from a current health check.

Normal use should rarely require Activity or Technical details. Those surfaces should help diagnose an exception. Overview should carry enough information to continue.

For performance, Defender is currently a hypothesis from the test notes. We need to identify where the time goes before choosing a fix. Measure navigation and input while artwork is busy, warm startup, cold game reads, and cached reads separately.

**The finish gate**

I would call the candidate ready only after these pass:

- Fresh setup reaches a real playable game without verbal guidance.
- Returning startup restores the expected server, folders, and integration.
- Library enumeration downloads no ROM content; a cold read works and a warm read demonstrably reuses cached data.
- Artwork activity leaves navigation and input responsive, and completion appears without changing pages.
- A removed RetroBat link produces an accurate affected-system warning and a safe repair path.
- Server interruption, file-access waits, stop, tray close/reopen, and explicit Quit produce truthful states and recover appropriately.
- Any sync feature included in the release passes its own transfer and conflict-preservation checks using test copies.
- One final unguided walkthrough needs no explanation from us. Every point where you hesitate becomes a candidate blocker.

Two days requires a hard priority order: **data safety and broken play paths first, false status second, responsiveness third, presentation cleanup fourth.** If an optional feature cannot meet its acceptance gate, narrow the release claim rather than marking it complete.

No files changed. I inspected source and existing evidence; I did not run the app, tests, or a Windows performance capture.  
The main uncertainty is whether native runtime defects fit the deadline; the first Windows session needs to establish that.
